This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Priyamvada Sharma, who is wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner No.2, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 12-04-2023 at about 4.25 p.m., the deceased Priyamvada Sharma was traveling in a car bearing No.KA-05- B-5480, along with her husband and son, the same was driven by her son slowly, carefully, cautiously, by observing all the vehicular Vineet Sharma vs Rakesh Kumar on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9564023/
2 movements, from Verna to Cansualim market.

When they reached near Three Kings Open Air Hall, Cansualim, Goa, the driver of the Eicher Tipper vehicle bearing No.GA-06-T-7950 came from Cansualim market to Verna side in rash and negligent manner, went on the other lane of the road and dashed against the car of the deceased.
Due to the impact, the deceased and inmates of the car have sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Goa Medical College, Bambolim, Goa, wherein she succumbed to fatal injuries on 13-04-2023 at about 00:30 hours.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was having her own business of supply of spare parts and allied products to buses to the Department of KSRTC and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Verna Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Eicher Tipper vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 24% per annum.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.3 has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.
Whereas, the respondents No.1 and 2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are placed as ex-parte.
4. The respondent No.3 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of the goods vehicle bearing No.GA-06-T-7950 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Section 147 and 150 of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provisions under Sections 134(C) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has sought permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2, as per Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the driver of the car was solely responsible for the accident and in fact the driver of the goods vehicle bearing No.GA-06-T-7950 was no way responsible for the death of the deceased.
Further it is contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.

It has denied the age,
income and avocation of the deceased.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05-B-5480 are not made as parties to the proceedings.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)

19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, "The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.

According to Section 2(11) CPC, "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the Tractor and Trally bearing No.AP-03-AN-8690 & AP-03-AN-8712 estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.
Almost in similar terms is the definition of legal representative under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 i.e. under Section 2(1)(g).

As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.

entities.text: Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".

As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child.

entities.text: Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.

In the concurring judgment of Vineet Sharma vs Rakesh Kumar on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9564023/
7
Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.
Indeed, in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

20. According to the ratio laid down in above decision, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

In order to determine the compensation, the age,
avocation, income, dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
21. The compensation towards loss of dependency:
The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased Priyamvada Sharma.

The petitioners have averred in the petition that, the deceased was having her own business of supply of spare parts and allied products to buses to the Department of KSRTC and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family and due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, they are struggling for their livelihood.
The same has been deposed by P.W.1 in his examination-in-chief affidavit.
The petitioners are claiming that, they were depending on the income of the deceased.

But, the P.W.1 in his cross-examination has clearly admitted that, he is an income tax assesse and he supplying the spare parts to BMTC, KSRTC, NWKSRTC and others, he is running the business in the name and style KARAN Trading Company and last year his annual income was about Rs.7,50,000/-.

Further,
he has clearly admitted that, his son/petitioner No.2 is working in Goa and his monthly income is about Rs.50,000/-.

This clearly goes to show that, as on the date of death of Priyamvada Sharma,
the petitioners were not depending on the income of deceased.

But, the Hon'ble Apex Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, has clearly held that, the legal representatives though not fully dependent on the deceased are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e.,
under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

22. sentences.text: 23. In the above cited decisions, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka and Hon'ble Apex Court has clearly held that, the major earning member, having independent source of income and living separately cannot be considered as a dependent of the deceased member of the family.
In the present case, admittedly, the petitioner No.2 is major, aged about 25 years, he is working in Goa and getting monthly income of Rs.50,000/-.

In such circumstances, in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decisions, this Court is of the opinion that, as on the date of death of Priyamvada Sharma, the petitioner No.2 was not the dependent of deceased.

Hence, the petitioner No.1, being the husband of deceased Priyamvada Sharma is alone considered as the dependent of the deceased and he is entitled for compensation under the head of loss of dependency.
In order to calculate the loss of dependency, the first step is to determine the age and income of the deceased.
i) Age and income of the deceased: The petitioners have averred that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 53 years.
To substantiate this point, the petitioners have not produced any document.
But, in Ex.P.6 post-mortem report and Ex.P.7 memorandum of autopsy, the age of the deceased is mentioned as 53 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased is considered as 53 years.

It is averred in the petition that, as on the date of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was having her own business of supply of spare parts and allied products to buses to the Department of KSRTC and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
To substantiate the same, they have produced Income Tax Returns for the year 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022- 23 of the deceased, which are marked as Ex.P.11 to 13.
As per Ex.P.11 to 13
Income Tax Returns for the year 2020-21, 2021-22 and 2022-23
, the annual net income of the deceased is Rs.4,40,236/-, Rs.4,43,930/- and Rs.4,81,900/- per annum respectively.
The accident has taken place on 12-04- 2023.

As there is some increase in the income of the deceased year on year, the net income of the deceased in the last preceding year of her death i.e.
2022-23 is considered as the income of deceased Priyamvada Sharma and her income is held at Rs.4,81,900/- per annum.

ii) As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the legal heirs of deceased are also entitled for future prospects of the deceased, though she was not a permanent employee as on the Vineet Sharma vs Rakesh Kumar on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/9564023/

Therefore, the future prospects of the deceased is held as Rs.48,190/-.

If this income is added to the notional income,
then it comes to Rs.5,30,090/-.
iii) The deduction of personal expenses and calculating the multiplier: The family of the deceased consist of two person i.e., petitioner No.1 & 2.
But, the total number of the dependents of the deceased is one.
Therefore, deduction towards the personal expenses of deceased is taken as 50% of the total income, which comes to Rs.2,65,045/-.
After deducting 50% out of total income, towards the personal expenses of deceased, the annual income of the deceased is held as Rs.2,65,045/-.
iv) As on the date of death, the age of the deceased was 53 years.

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 S.C., the appropriate multiplier in the present case is taken as 11.

In the present case, admittedly the petitioner No.1 is husband and petitioner No.2 is son of deceased Priyamvada Sharma

As per the guidelines laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680, the compensation under the following conventional heads is awarded:

25. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.

Further, the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending Eicher Tipper vehicle bearing Reg. No. GA-06-T-7950, the accident in question has occurred and deceased Priyamvada Sharma has succumbed to the grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.3 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Priyamvada Sharma, who is wife of petitioner No.1 and mother of petitioner No.2, in a road traffic accident.
Due to the impact, the deceased and inmates of the car have sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the deceased was shifted to Goa Medical College, Bambolim, Goa, wherein she succumbed to fatal injuries on 13-04-2023 at about 00:30 hours.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was having her own business of supply of spare parts and allied products to buses to the Department of KSRTC and was earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- per month.
She was contributing her entire earnings to her family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Verna Police have registered the case against the driver of the said Eicher Tipper vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 337 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the driver, respondent No.2 is the owner and respondent No.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the car bearing No.KA-05-B-5480 are not made as parties to the proceedings.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
